note: English and Spanish Wikipedia describe the cave paintings of Ahuila Gencha Machay (Singa, Huanuco) and their location but give no date; no readable source dates them.
Askeladden gives Bronze Age only as a register category and no source dates the two elk carvings to a year.

The English Wikipedia article dates the Dulan site only as 'The site and objects date back to 3,000 years ago', and the Chinese article likewise says only '距今約3000年' (about 3,000 years ago). A year worked out from 'years ago' is not read, so no source states a calendar year, century or millennium for the start.
The only dating found (Northamptonshire HER: early 2nd to 4th century) is on a page the quote check cannot read; no readable source dates the start.
The English article of the item carries no coordinate line, and the Wikidata item Q15949954 states no P625 coordinate at all, so no source can be quoted that gives a point for Titiqaqa in Cusco.
The English article of the item dates nothing; it only places the site in the Cusco Region, and the Wikidata item carries no inception statement, so no source gives a start year for the site itself.

The only printed point found (Megalithic Portal, 16.858721N 96.695741W) is 2 km from the stored point and coincides with the centre of the town San Martín Tilcajete (Wikipedia 16.8589, -96.695), so it is the nearest-town point, not the site's; no source prints a point for the El Palenque hillside site itself.
Sources date the nine stone tools only to the Middle Paleolithic, a period word with no year, century or millennium in BC form.
The readable pages (Wikipedia) give no start date; the excavators' papers say only Preclassic/Middle Preclassic without a year and are not readable by plain GET.
Wikipedia marks the coordinates as missing and Wikidata has no P625; no readable source found gives a point for Llaqta Qulluy in Vilca.
No readable source dates Llaqta Qulluy in Vilca; Wikipedia only gives the name's meaning.

The only printed points are for the village El Cedral (Wikipedia/Wikidata 20.3658, -86.9939), not for the Maya ruin itself; no source prints a point for the site, so the stored point cannot be confirmed.

The 1st century AD appears only as a hedged statement in Arabic Wikipedia and on Archiqoo, with identical wording, no primary source; the Algerian heritage map's own record says the bridge dates to the Berber period (no year), so no reliable source dates the start.

Wikipedia and the Kent Archaeological Society paper only say the sarsens may be the remains of a Neolithic monument or a recent collection of natural stones; no year, century or millennium is given for the start.

Sources disagree on what the site is (moated manor farm, spring with scattered sarsens that may be natural stones rather than genuine megaliths); no source states one type firmly enough to choose a canonical type.

No readable source prints a point for the Xihuatoxtla Shelter itself: the PNAS paper (Ranere et al. 2009) gives only elevation and distance from a barranca, the Wikipedia Balsas River point is the river's, and the Megalithic Portal page is behind a bot challenge.

No readable source gives a point for Bruach an Druimein: the Ireland Calls record prints only an OS grid reference, which is not read, the Canmore record refuses automated requests and the Archaeology Data Service volume page is likewise refused.

The excavation summary says only that the earlier features may be of earlier date and that glass beads date the later phases to the second half of the first millennium AD; that is the site's later phases in period terms and no source gives a year, century or millennium for the start of the site.

No source gives a point for the Mihailovac site near Vršac. The English Wikipedia article carries no coordinates and the Wikidata item Q6845188 has no coordinate statement; the Digital Atlas point that exists belongs to another Mihailovac 128 km away, so no source can be quoted for this site's point.

English and Spanish Wikipedia record only the 2003 heritage declaration of Chipaw Marka (Chipaomarca, Chipao, Lucanas) and local pages say only pre-Inca and Inca; no source gives a year, century or millennium for its start.

No readable page prints a point for Careyeros Hill itself: the Megalithic Portal entry is behind a bot challenge (HTTP 403), Wikipedia's Punta Mita article gives only the resort town's point (20.7752, -105.527), and Nominatim only finds Playa Careyeros and a street.
Wikipedia marks the coordinates as missing and Wikidata has no P625; no readable source found gives a point for Llaqta Qulluy in Acoria.
No readable source dates Llaqta Qulluy in Acoria; Wikipedia only gives the name's meaning.

The only readable source (the MINCETUR tourism inventory record, in Spanish) calls it a pre-Hispanic settlement (asentamiento) of terraces, platforms and circular building remains, but no English-readable source states a canonical type, so the type is left for the owner.
Neither Wikipedia (English or Spanish), Wikidata nor the MINCETUR tourism inventory record gives a point for Qurimarka in Apurimac; no readable source with coordinates was found.

No source prints a point for Pusuquy Pata (Posoqoypata/Chillicopampa): Wikipedia, Wikidata and the Valdez et al. excavation paper only place it on a hill by the Huanta-Luricocha road, about 15 km north of Wari.
The excavation paper dates the cemetery only by relative period (Middle Horizon epoch 1B to epoch 2) without any calendar year or century, which does not date the start.

The only published coordinates (Wikipedia, Wikidata) are those of the mountain T'akaq; local tourism text puts the archaeological site on the hill about 500 m from Chavinillo, which lies about 3.5 km from the stored point, so no source gives the site's own point.
No readable source dates the archaeological site of T'akaq.
The only dating found is the period word Intermedio Tardio (Late Intermediate) without any year or century, which does not date the start.
No readable source prints a point for the Tomb of Ramhai; only the Northern Stelae Field as a whole has a printed point, which is not the tomb.
The only date found (a stela of Ramhai said to date from 2500 B.C.) comes from a personal travel blog and is not a dating of the tomb; no reliable source dates it.
No article, register entry or scholarly page about the Tomb of Ramhai itself could be found; only a stock-photo caption names it.
No readable source prints a point for the colossus itself (Digital Karnak gives only the place, fronting the 2nd Pylon at Karnak); the stored point stays.
The page about this colossus (Digital Karnak) spells the name Ramesses and has no title matching the stored name; the Italian Wikipedia article covers all colossi of Ramses II, not this one.

The Wikipedia article and Wikidata item print no coordinates. Literature on Chevdar (Chavdar, Pirdop area) points to the tell by Chavdar village in Sofia Province, which conflicts with the article's 'near Kazanluk' and the stored point (Kazanlak town), but no page prints a point for the site itself.

English Wikipedia says only 'Neolithic' and 'early Neolithic' (a period word). Sources with a year concern the Chavdar tell in Sofia Province, whose identity with the article's 'near Kazanluk' site is not established, so no source dates this site.

Wikipedia and Wikidata give no point for Presa-Tusiu; the only printed point found is a hobbyist photo page that writes it with doubled apostrophes, which is not a readable coordinate form, and the excavation reports give no point.
